descriptions.mandarin_vocabulary: This deck is the main deck for practicing vocabulary. It either asks you to guess the character from the pinyin and definition, or the pinyin from the character and definition, or the definition from the character and pinyin.
descriptions.mandarin_writing: This deck is for practicing writing only. It asks you to guess the characters from the definition and pinyin. Only characters with “written known” ticked will be part of this deck.

ankiConnectGuideModal.title: Set up AnkiConnect
ankiConnectGuideModal.description: Teacher Wang talks to Anki through the AnkiConnect add-on. Follow these steps, then close this guide to re-check the connection.

createAccount.title: Create an Anki account
createAccount.description: Go to ankiweb.net and create a free account so you can sync decks across devices later.

installDesktop.title: Install Anki desktop
installDesktop.description: Download and install the Anki desktop app for your operating system from apps.ankiweb.net, then open it and sign in if prompted.

openAddons.title: Open Anki add-ons
openAddons.description: In Anki, open Tools → Add-ons → Get Add-ons… to install new plugins.

installAddon.title: Install AnkiConnect
installAddon.description: Enter the add-on code 2055492159 and confirm. Restart Anki when prompted.
installAddon.imageAlt: Anki Get Add-ons dialog with code 2055492159

allowCors.title: Allow browser access (CORS)
allowCors.description: In Anki, open Tools → Add-ons → AnkiConnect → Config and set webCorsOriginList to ["*"] (or include http://localhost:5173). Restart Anki so Teacher Wang can call AnkiConnect from the app.

verify.title: Verify the connection
verify.description: Keep Anki open in the background, then open http://localhost:8765 in a browser. You should see the text “AnkiConnect”. Close this guide to refresh the connection status.

ankiSyncHelpModal.title: Anki synchronization gotchas
ankiSyncHelpModal.bullet1: Make sure your Anki cards have a "definition" (they cannot be imported if this field is empty).
ankiSyncHelpModal.bullet2: Make sure your Anki cards have the correct syntax for pinyin: should have either the "pinyin" or the "numerical" format. If a card is composed of several pinyins, they should be split by a space.
ankiSyncHelpModal.bullet3: Make sure, if you haven't set the pinyin for this card, that the pinyin of the character can be detected automatically from another card.

overview.lead: Choose a direction. Push sends local knowledge-base content to Anki. Pull imports Anki cards into the app.

push.title: Push to Anki
push.copy: One-way only: add new local cards to this Anki deck, or ignore them so they are not offered again.
push.allSet: You’re all set, nothing to push.
push.unsyncableText: These words are missing a definition or pinyin, so a card cannot be built for them: <1>{{words}}</1>. You can skip them with “Ignore all for push”.

pull.title: Pull from Anki
pull.copyWriting: Words found in this Anki deck that exist in your knowledge base but are not yet marked as “written known”.
pull.copyNonWriting: Cards found in this Anki deck that are not yet in your knowledge base.
pull.allSet: You’re all set, nothing to pull.
pull.missingWritingTitle: Words not yet in the knowledge base
pull.missingWritingText: These words from Anki don’t exist in your knowledge base yet. Add them manually in the app, synchronize the Mandarin vocabulary deck with them first, or ignore them for future pulls: <1>{{words}}</1>.
pull.missingNonWritingText: These Anki cards contain Chinese characters whose pinyin could not be resolved from the deck: <1>{{words}}</1>.

partial.pushMessage: Choose which cards to push to Anki. Unselected cards will be ignored for future pushes.
partial.pullMessageWriting: Choose which words to mark as “written known”. Unselected words will be ignored for future pulls.
partial.pullMessageNonWriting: Choose which cards to pull from Anki. Unselected cards will be ignored for future pulls.
